title: fix(core): ValueDataSource refuses an empty operator map in an object $filter (objectui#10817)
body:
Fixes #10817
Clause-②: no — the value path starts refusing a shape objectstack#5240 ruled refused, and comparands the spec's `ACCEPTED_FILTER_COMPARAND_TYPES` rules out (objectui#8567); on this face both only ever dropped a constraint — as PR objectui#10810 did on the converter path; no declared surface moves.

Implements seat ruling `5858511329` (Q1 = A2, filter-level exclude-and-log; Q2 dissolved), which answers the round-1 `needs_decision` report `5858469332`. Claim `5858403682`, session `session_014mXUNuFomfj24w7s1pZzhN`. Per the ruling, the claim's `filter-converter.ts` line narrows to "not touched".

## What changed

- `ValueDataSource.find`, object arm: before `matchesFilter` runs, a new helper `zeroKeyConditionRefusal` walks the filter's field entries and recurses into the members of `$and` / `$or`. It follows the same two combinators `matchesFilter` executes. A field whose condition is a non-null, non-array object with no own keys is handed to `toFilterNodeSafely({ [field]: condition })`. That symbol was already public and already imported. On the first `{ ok: false, refusal }`, the arm runs `refuseFilterNode(refusals, loweringRefusalReason(refusal))` and sets `result = []`, the array arm's objectui#10767 shape. The existing drain loop logs the one warning. Otherwise `matchesFilter` runs exactly as before. `find` never rejects.
- `loweringRefusalReason`'s docblock names its second caller. No other code in the file moved.
- `packages/core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts` is not touched, so there is no new export (`@object-ui/core` re-exports that whole module). The converter alone decides what an empty operator map is, with its own throw site and its own wording.
- New `ValueDataSource.emptyOperatorMap-10817.test.ts` (16 cases).
- `.changeset/10817-value-source-empty-operator-map.md`: `'@object-ui/core': patch`, with a `Clause-②: no` paragraph. It declares the refusal of a zero-key exotic comparand (a `RegExp`, `Map`, `Set`, `URL` or class instance with no own fields) the routing carries.
- File-surface addition beyond the claim, declared here: the adapters README gains the section "An empty operator map refuses the whole filter" (AGENTS.md #2). It is 13 added lines, all prose.

## H1 — reproduced on `main` (base `fb91ac9b0c`), both paths

Rows `[{id:'1',status:'a',created:'x'},{id:'2',status:'a'},{id:'3',status:'b'}]`, from a throwaway probe that was not committed.

| filter | `ValueDataSource.find` on base | `convertFiltersToAST` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `{ status: 'a', created: {} }` | ids `1,2`, 0 warns | throws `FilterOperatorError`, `INVALID_FILTER` / 400, field `created` |
| `{ created: {} }` | ids `1,2,3`, 0 warns | same refusal |
| `{ $and: [{ status: 'a', created: {} }] }` | ids `1,2`, 0 warns | same refusal |
| `{ $and: [{ created: {} }] }` | ids `1,2,3`, 0 warns | same refusal |
| `{ $or: [{ created: {} }] }` | ids `1,2,3`, 0 warns | same refusal |
| `{ $or: [{ status: 'b' }, { status: 'a', created: {} }] }` | ids `1,2,3`, 0 warns | same refusal |
| CONTROL `{ status: 'a' }` | ids `1,2` | `['status','=','a']` |

The converter's message begins "[ObjectUI] The filter on field 'created' is an EMPTY operator map".

## H2 — the envelope

- **The object arm's sibling refusals** go through `refuseFilterNode`. It adds "[ObjectUI] ValueDataSource: REASON. Rows are excluded rather than passed through." to the `refusals` Set, per node, and `find` drains the Set once with `console.warn`. Measured for `{ status: { $foo: 1 } }`: ids `[]` and one warning, "filter operator '$foo' on field 'status' is not implemented by the in-memory matcher".
- **The array arm's lowering refusal** is `const lowered = toFilterNodeSafely(params.$filter); if (!lowered.ok) { refuseFilterNode(refusals, loweringRefusalReason(lowered.refusal)); result = []; }`. It is filter-level, and `find` resolves.
- **Ruling A2** puts the empty map in that same Set with the array arm's filter-level shape. `find` resolves `{ data: [], total: 0 }` with exactly one warning. The body of that warning is the converter's own message, with its prefix and closing period taken off by `loweringRefusalReason`. Per node (option A) was rejected because it is row-dependent: `$or` would still answer row 3. Throwing (option B) is objectui#8600's Q1, which stays unruled.

## H3 — where the arm sits

- It runs in `find`'s object arm, after the `Object.keys(params.$filter).length > 0` guard and before any row is matched. It runs up front because `matchesFilter` returns on a row's first false entry and `$or` uses `some()`, so a refusal raised while matching would depend on the row.
- The converter's own order is kept by construction. `convertFiltersToAST` runs its Date arm, then its exotic-comparand arm (via its private `isOperatorMap`), then its empty-map arm. `isOperatorMap` is reused by routing, not by export. The value face had no Date or exotic-comparand arm of its own.
- Controls that must not refuse: a `null` / `undefined` condition is not an object and is not routed. The `{}` whole filter never reaches the arm because of the guard above. `$not` and other `$` keys are skipped, so they keep their existing refusals. An object that has keys is not routed and is still judged per node.
- `$and` / `$or` members reach the same check through the walk's recursion, which mirrors `matchesLogicalGroup`. A malformed group (not an array, or a member that is not an object) is left to `matchesLogicalGroup`'s refusal.
- `$or`'s early TRUE return in `lowerLogicalGroup` is not changed (objectui#10789 owns it). See Acceptance notes.

## Pins and ablation

The test file is `ValueDataSource.emptyOperatorMap-10817.test.ts`. The refusal pins assert `data` / `ids` `[]`, `total: 0`, and `warns` equal to exactly `[expected]`. `expected` is the adapter's lowering frame around the converter's live message for the SAME whole filter, read from `toFilterNodeSafely` and compared as a string.

- §1: `{ status: 'a', created: {} }` and `{ created: {} }`.
- §2: the two `$and` forms and the two `$or` forms, including `{ $or: [{ status: 'b' }, { status: 'a', created: {} }] }`, which answers empty, not row 3.
- §3: a `RegExp`, a `Map` and a `Set` comparand (`{ status: 'a', created: X }`). Each is refused with the converter's exotic-comparand wording (objectui#8567).
- §4, controls that answer the same on base and head:
  - `{ status: 'a' }` answers `1,2`;
  - `{ created: null }` answers `[]`;
  - the `{}` whole filter answers `1,2,3`;
  - `{ status: 'a', created: new Date(0) }` answers `1,2`. This is today's answer, pinned as-is, with a comment naming the seat's follow-up card;
  - a real operator beside the key answers `1`;
  - the `$foo` sibling is still excluded per node, with its own sentence.
- §5: the array arm's lowering refusal carries the same frame, so this is one envelope, not a second one.

Red on base: the new file ran against `ValueDataSource.ts` restored to base (blob `6cc8754cd3`), using a trap-guarded script. It read `Tests  9 failed | 7 passed (16)`.
- The 9 red rows are §1 (2), §2 (4) and §3 (3). Each failed with `expected [ '1', '2' ]` or `expected [ '1', '2', '3' ] to deeply equal []`.
- All 6 controls and §5 stayed green.
- The restore was proven: the blob after restore equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

Ablation, on head `2f13b0ff27`: `ablation-replace.mjs` replaced `const refusal = zeroKeyConditionRefusal(filter);` with `const refusal = undefined;`.
- The tool reported anchor x1 to x0, replacement x0 to x1, and the blob changing from `d28c1ed58c` to `f67c0ef80a`. On-disk grep gave injected=1 and removed-anchor=0.
- The run read `Tests  9 failed | 7 passed (16)`, with the same 9 rows as on base and every control green.
- The tool restored the file and reported `blob == HEAD (d28c1ed58cf1) and git diff HEAD is empty`.
- The direction was predicted in the test header before the run, and it matched. The test imports `../ValueDataSource` from source, so no `dist/` is involved.

## Gates (head `2f13b0ff27`)

- ② `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core type-check` gave `VERDICT command-exit 0`. `--listFiles` counts the new test file (1) in `tsconfig.test.json` and `ValueDataSource.ts` (1) in `tsconfig.json`.
- ② `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/core/ scripts/__tests__/dollar-dialect-alias-census.test.ts` gave `Test Files  180 passed (180)`, `Tests  3621 passed (3621)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- Targeted `eslint --no-inline-config` on the two touched `.ts` files gave `0 errors`. Every warning is pre-existing in `ValueDataSource.ts`: net new `any` is zero, and the test file has none. This is not a narrowing claim; repo-wide lint is CI's.

- `check-new-cross-file-line-citations`: "VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)".

- `check-changeset-overwrite`: "No pre-existing changeset was modified or deleted." (at the round-2 head; since round 3 it reports the appended `8513` dated note as its case 2, a correction on purpose, frontmatter untouched)

## Serial

- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` against a fresh `origin/main` `fda49e557b` exits 0, tree `cbf014b9de`.
- objectui#10789's PR objectui#10830 is open (head `664305cb32`). `git merge-tree --write-tree` against it exits 0, tree `7893b15d1c`. That PR touches `filter-converter.ts` (the `absorbed` flag in `lowerLogicalGroup`) and not `ValueDataSource.ts`. This PR does not touch `filter-converter.ts`.
- None of the other 9 open PRs touches `ValueDataSource.ts`, the adapters README or `filter-converter.ts`, read from each PR's file list. The release PR (5400) was not read, because its 100-file list may be truncated.

## Acceptance notes

- **Pending changesets read against this diff:** `9164-empty-operator-map-refused`, `10788-empty-operator-map-beside-key-refused`, `8555-filter-converter-date-comparand`, `8567-filter-converter-exotic-comparand` and `identity-fold-skipped-keys-9030`. Each describes `convertFiltersToAST` and its callers only. None says the value path widens or that only the converter refuses, so none became false. None is touched and no dated note is added.
- **Rounds 3 and 4 (contract review `5858803986`, text only).** `.changeset/8513-value-datasource-grouped-filters.md` gains a dated note in the objectui#10533 form: its "a `{}` branch is a TRUE disjunct that absorbs its `$or`" is this change's reading, since `{ $or: [{}, { created: {} }] }` now answers no rows on this face. The frontmatter is byte-identical. The README section and the `10817` changeset are scoped: the field is judged alone; the walk does not look under `$not`; `URL` and class instances are declared; a `Date`'s constraint still vanishes (objectui#10829); and a mixed filter logs only the walk's refusal. The `ValueDataSource.ts` JSDoc gets comment lines only.
- **`check-changeset-claims`** names two pending bodies that cite the adapters README: `6213-core-adapters-readme-owns-its-directory` ("now documents the adapters that are actually in that directory") and `8976-icontains-lowers-in-converter` ("prescribes it as the repair when `$like` / `$ilike` / `$regex` are refused"). Both still hold.
- **`10767-value-data-source-rule-array-filter`** says "the `$`-dialect arm is untouched". That is that entry's reading of its own change, and it is outside the five this order names, so it is not edited.
- **Date:** `{ status: 'a', created: new Date(0) }` still answers rows 1 and 2 on this face. The Date constraint vanishes, while the converter lowers it to an equality. It is pinned as today's answer; the seat files that card separately.
- **`{ created: null }`:** this face answers `[]` (strict `=== null`), while the converter skips the key (objectui#9020). This is recorded on the card only and is unchanged.
- **`{ $or: [{}, { created: {} }] }`** (probe on head): this face now refuses it, because the walk does not depend on member order. The converter on `main` answers `undefined` (TRUE) through `lowerLogicalGroup`'s early return. After PR objectui#10830 lands, the converter converts every member before absorbing and refuses it too. This is not pinned here.
- **Mixed refusals:** `{ status: ['a'], created: {} }` is refused by both faces with no rows. This face names `created`, because the walk runs before the per-node refusals. The converter names `status`, its first loop refusal. This is not pinned.
- **Wording:** `loweringRefusalReason`'s frame reads "filter rule refused as it is lowered" for an object filter too. The ruling says to apply the array arm's shape exactly, so it is reused as-is.
- **Commit trailers** are model-free.
